name: Ernst Happel
scopeNote: Austrian manager (1925-1992). Counted spells: Feyenoord, Club Brugge, Netherlands (1978 World Cup), Hamburger SV. Sources name his style as an early form of pressing with quick passing (The Blizzard), a pressing 4-3-3 (These Football Times), a three-man midfield against the 4-2-4 (90min/SI), zonal marking (player quote, NOS). He is sometimes labelled a Total Football or Michels-style coach; sources instead place him as a separate figure (Israel: 'a very different type to Rinus Michels'). Exact start/end days of spells come from search summaries of Wikipedia-type pages (not read in a digest): see openQuestions. Quotes without a known date are in statedView with date 'undated'. Excluded-spell years (1962, 1969, 1973, 1975, 1979, 1981, 1987, 1991, 1992) are year-only because the exact days were not found.
openQuestions: Spell dates are not verified in any digest paragraph: Feyenoord 1969-08-01 to 1973-05-30, Club Brugge 1974-01-23 to 1978-10-26, Hamburg 1981-07-01 to 1987-06-30 come from Wikipedia-type search summaries (the infobox says they are first and last matches, not contract dates). Digests confirm only: Brugge appointed January 1974 (The Blizzard) and he left in November 1978 (The Blizzard) vs 26 October 1978 (summary); Netherlands from May 1977 (NOS). Check Brugge exit (Oct vs Nov 1978).

Netherlands 1978: The World Soccer article (2014) says Jan Zwartkruis took over tactics and preparation after the group stage and Happel became a figurehead; Wildschut is quoted crediting Zwartkruis. Credit for the 1978 tactical choices is contested, so Netherlands facts are weak evidence of Happel's own style. Netherlands end date set to the final (1978-06-25), start 1977-05-01 is a month-level date from NOS ('vanaf mei 1977').

Pressing origin: FourFourTwo (via Uli Hesse) says Happel used pressing at Hamburg; the Blizzard calls it an early form of pressing at Brugge; 90min lists Maslov as innovator. No source found with tactical analysis (movement, line height, triggers) for Feyenoord 1969-73 or Hamburg beyond one-line descriptions.

Feyenoord zonal marking rests on one player quote (Van Duivenbode, NOS 2020). Hamburg 1983 final: Wilson via TFT says Gentile was told to man-mark Bastrup (Juventus man-marking), while Happel's own side marking system is not described. A search summary (not read) says he asked players whether to man-mark Platini: unverified.
Quotes 'Gentlemen, two points' and 'A day without football is a day wasted' have no primary source found (attributed).

Excluded spells not researched: ADO Den Haag 1962-69 (1968 KNVB Cup win over Ajax, 4-3-3 against 4-2-4 per TFT; domestic cup only, taken as the step towards Feyenoord), Sevilla 1973-75 (second-division spell, 'uneventful' per 90min), Standard Liege 1979-81 (Belgian Cup, few tactical sources), Swarovski Tirol 1987-91 (two Austrian titles, almost no tactical coverage found), Austria 1992 (under a year, died November 1992, few matches). Swarovski Tirol could be added if the user wants the four-country titles in scope.
set-pieces: no verified fact in-period (only a Hrubesch 2000 quote about Bananenflanke-Kopf, not a set piece); statedView dates are article dates where the quote is undated.
